elements.label: Figure 2.8
elements.description: Stacked column chart of the share of workers (%) by sector, split into 'Has contract' (2010, 2020) and 'No contract' (2010, 2020) groups. Y-axis: Share of workers (%), 0 to 100. Legend series: Agriculture and fishing; Electricity, gas and water; Education, health and social work; Financial, insurance and real estate; Mining and quarrying; Construction; Transport, storage, and comms; Other; Manufacturing; Commerce; Public admin. Printed values: Has contract 2010: Public admin 14.8, Education, health and social work 19.1, Manufacturing 32.8. Has contract 2020: Public admin 9.3, Education, health and social work 14.9, Manufacturing 46.6. No contract 2010: Agriculture and fishing 56.2, Manufacturing 12.8, Commerce 17.0. No contract 2020: Agriculture and fishing 40.4, Manufacturing 15.9, Commerce 23.1. Unlabeled segments (small mining, construction, transport, other) are not printed. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010–2020. The pattern shows agriculture dominating non-contract jobs, with its share falling from ~56 to ~40 percent between 2010 and 2020, while contracted jobs are concentrated in manufacturing and public or service sectors.

elements.label: Figure 2.9
elements.description: Two-panel line chart of underemployment and unemployment rates, 2010 to 2020, from GSO. Panel A, 'Underemployment rate': y-axis Underemployment (%), 0 to 6; series General, 15–24, 25–49, 50+, Male, Female. Approximate readings for 15–24: ~5.1 (2010), ~4.2, ~4.3, ~3.8, ~3.4, ~3.6, ~2.8, ~2.7, ~2.4, ~2.4, ~4.1 (2020). Other series mostly fall from ~3.5 in 2010 to ~1.5–2.0 by 2018–2019 and rise to ~2.5 in 2020; 50+ is ~3.1 in 2010, ~0.9 in 2019 and ~1.9 in 2020. Panel B, 'Unemployment rate': y-axis Unemployment (%) (labelled Underemployment on the axis), 0 to 8; series General, 15–24, 25–49, 50+, Male, Female. Approximate readings for 15–24: ~7.1 (2010), ~5.2, ~5.5, ~6.2, ~6.3, ~7.1, ~7.4, ~7.4, ~6.9, ~6.5, ~7.2 (2020). General ~2.9 (2010) falling to ~1.9–2.3 and ~2.5 in 2020; Female ~3.5 (2010) and ~3.1 (2020); 25–49 ~1.8 falling to ~1.2–1.5 and ~2.0 in 2020; 50+ ~0.7–1.0 from 2015 onward. Pattern: youth (15–24) unemployment and underemployment are highest and rise in 2020, while the other groups show a clear uptick in 2020.
